=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- `scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh`:95 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The subset check compares raw narrative paths to committed paths without path normalization.
  WHY: Equivalent paths such as `./.ai/review_issue_ledger/pr-1524.txt` and `.ai/review_issue_ledger/pr-1524.txt` will not match under exact string comparison, causing false `EDITOR_CHANGES_LOST` reports.
- `scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh`:83-98 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The narrative-path extraction regex can capture non-file backticked strings and other non-path text.
  WHY: Backticked identifiers or command snippets can enter `narrative_paths` and fail the subset check even when the actual edited file set is correct, creating false positives; one reviewer noted this is partially mitigated by the edit-verb filter and file-extension requirement.
- `agents.md`:568 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The documentation incorrectly attributes `COMMITTED_FILES_FILE` being wired into the step environment to `scripts/review_commit_changes.sh`.
  WHY: The variable is actually set by the workflow’s “Initialize runtime workspace” step in `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`; `scripts/review_commit_changes.sh` only reads and writes the file path, so the doc misstates the source.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- `scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh`:95 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Path extraction regex strips leading dots from file paths.
  WHY: Paths like `.ai/review_issue_ledger/pr-1524.txt` become `ai/review_issue_ledger/pr-1524.txt`, causing mismatch when compared with committed paths.
- `scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh`:95 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The regex captures any backtick-enclosed text, not just file paths.
  WHY: Non-file strings extracted from narrative fail the subset check and trigger false `EDITOR_CHANGES_LOST` positives.
- `scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh`:95 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The file extension pattern `\.[A-Za-z]{1,6}` is too restrictive.
  WHY: Common files with longer extensions or no extensions will not be extracted, which can produce false positives.
- `scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh`:103 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Path comparison does not normalize equivalent path spellings before exact matching.
  WHY: Variants like `.ai/...`, `./.ai/...`, and `.ai//...` will not match under `grep -qxF`, causing false mismatches.
- `agents.md`:568 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The documentation says `COMMITTED_FILES_FILE` is already wired into the step env by `scripts/review_commit_changes.sh`.
  WHY: The file is initialized in workflow YAML and written by `scripts/review_commit_changes.sh`, so the attribution is incorrect.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===
- `agents.md`:568 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The documentation incorrectly states that `COMMITTED_FILES_FILE` is already wired into the step env by `scripts/review_commit_changes.sh`.
  WHY: `scripts/review_commit_changes.sh` is a consumer/writer of the file path, not the provider of the environment variable, so the doc misleads maintainers.
- `scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh`:83-91 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The regex and grep logic for extracting `narrative_paths` is too greedy and captures non-path strings, especially when enclosed in backticks.
  WHY: Backticked code symbols or commands can be extracted as paths, and then fail the subset check, producing a false-positive `EDITOR_CHANGES_LOST` warning.
- `scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh`:95 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Comparison between extracted `nar_path` and `committed_paths` lacks path normalization.
  WHY: Paths with leading `./` or similar spellings will not match the committed list under exact string comparison, causing incorrect lost-change reports.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- `scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh`:103 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The subset check uses exact string matching without normalizing paths.
  WHY: Equivalent paths such as `./.ai/review_issue_ledger/pr-1524.txt` and `.ai/review_issue_ledger/pr-1524.txt` will not match, so legitimate commits can be misclassified as lost changes.
- `scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh`:95-98 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The regex extracts backticked content that is not necessarily a file path.
  WHY: The edit-verb filter reduces the risk, but an edit-verb line that also contains a command or identifier in backticks can still feed a non-path into the subset check.
- `agents.md`:568 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The docs misattribute `COMMITTED_FILES_FILE` to `scripts/review_commit_changes.sh`.
  WHY: The variable is actually set by the workflow’s “Initialize runtime workspace” step; the script only writes the committed-paths file.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- `agents.md`:568 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The documentation incorrectly attributes where `COMMITTED_FILES_FILE` is initially set.
  WHY: It is set by the workflow step in `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`, while `scripts/review_commit_changes.sh` only reads the env var and writes the file contents.
- `scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh`:94 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The subset check uses exact string matching between narrative paths and committed paths without normalization.
  WHY: A narrative path like `./.ai/review_issue_ledger/pr-1524.txt` will not match `.ai/review_issue_ledger/pr-1524.txt`, creating false positives.
- `scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh`:83-91 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The narrative path extraction regex could capture backticked identifiers that are not actual file paths.
  WHY: Although mitigated by the edit-verb filter and extension requirement, a backticked non-path string that resembles a file path can still enter the subset check and fail it.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
- `scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh`:~95 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The subset check compares raw narrative paths to committed paths without normalizing equivalent representations.
  WHY: Leading `./` or duplicate slashes in narrative paths will not match the committed file list under exact string comparison, so legitimate ledger-only commits can be misclassified as lost changes.
- `scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh`:~84-90 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The backtick capture pattern extracts any backticked content, including non-file identifiers and command snippets.
  WHY: These extracted strings are never present in `committed_paths`, so the subset check can fail and the script can return a false positive.
- `agents.md`:568 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The documentation incorrectly states that `COMMITTED_FILES_FILE` is wired into the step env by `scripts/review_commit_changes.sh`.
  WHY: The env var is set by the “Initialize runtime workspace” workflow step, and the script only reads or writes the file path, so the doc should be corrected.
=== END FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
